name: Question 12
problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+26y=0.
$$
worked_solution:
Let $y={e}^{\lambda x}.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}+2\lambda {e}^{\lambda x}+26{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +26) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +26=0.
$$

The auxiliary equation can be solved by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +26 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +1)-1+26 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2}+25 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2} & =-25 \\ \lambda +1 & =\pm 5\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-1\pm 5\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{-x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡5x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the general solution to the equation d2ydx2+2dydx+26y=0.

a
y=e−2x(Pcos⁡5x+Qsin⁡5x)
b
y=e−2x(Pcos⁡3x+Qsin⁡3x)
c
y=e−x(Pcos⁡5x+Qsin⁡5x)
d
y=e−x(Pcos⁡3x+Qsin⁡3x)
e
y=ex(Pcos⁡5x+Qsin⁡5x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let y=eλx. Differentiating y with respect to x gives

dydx=λeλx,d2ydx2=λ2eλx.

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

λ2eλx+2λeλx+26eλx=0eλx(λ2+2λ+26)=0.

The auxiliary equation is therefore

λ2+2λ+26=0.

The auxiliary equation can be solved by completing the square:

λ2+2λ+26=0(λ2+2λ+1)−1+26=0(λ+1)2+25=0(λ+1)2=−25λ+1=±5iλ=−1±5i

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation is

y=e−x(Pcos⁡5x+Qsin⁡5x).
